text:
sam (oncall): noticed a spike in Pending GPU pods in us-east-1 starting ~08:12UTC. scheduler shows InsufficientResource for nvidia.com/gpu even though node pool reports free capacity. this is affecting dedicated lanes for a few customers. pinging eng-sre.

katie (eng-sre): looking. can you paste the scheduler events? any change around kubelet/nvidia-driver?

sam (oncall): pasted events to thread. main repeating error: "failed to allocate device: driver version mismatch" and a couple of nodes moved to NotReady during the window. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc/provisioning?orgId=1

raj (eng-runtime): that driver mismatch rings a bell — we had a rolling driver update last night in the pool with a bad rollout window. autoscaler still thinks nodes are available but kubelet/driver mismatch prevents kubelet from advertising GPUs.

maria (eng-platform): confirmed — controller logs show the node pool upgrade job rolled forward to 2 nodes that didn't run the preflight. nodes stayed Ready for CPU but exported zero gpus. suggests driver preflight race.

luis (eng-ml): customer jobs queued for >5m. would recommend short traffic shift to us-west-2 while we remediate to avoid SLA hits. cost vs latency tradeoff flagged.

sam (oncall): initiating controlled traffic shift for dedicated tenants in us-east-1 to us-west-2 using traffic-shift/v2 script. will hold cross-regional config for public customers.

monitoring-bot: alert: us-east-1 GPU provisioning error rate 34% (threshold 5%). incidents channel notified.

deploy-bot: started traffic-shift job id=ts-1749991111. rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks.

katie (eng-sre): remediation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) taint drain non-GPU workloads 3) re-run driver preflight + restart kubelet 4) uncordon and validate GPU allocatable. doing step 1 now.

raj (eng-runtime): quick command to detect affected nodes:
```
kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.allocatable["nvidia.com/gpu"]==null) | .metadata.name'
```
and to force preflight:
```
ssh node && sudo /opt/nvidia/preflight-check.sh && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```

maria (eng-platform): doing a rolling remediation with a 2m delay between nodes. will post when GPU allocatable returns. also creating a temporary warm pool in us-west-2 to absorb load once traffic shift completes.

luis (eng-ml): note — we should measure model latency change for those tenants. I'll add a synthetic test against the shifted traffic.

sam (oncall): traffic shift at 50% now, health is green for shifted requests. continuing remediation.

katie (eng-sre): after remediating 6 nodes allocatable is back. rollbacks stopped. moving to monitoring.

maria (eng-platform): marking the incident as mitigated. customers on dedicated lanes who were shifted report success.

sam (oncall): quick post-mortem notes / action items (to capture here):
- root cause: driver rolling update didn't validate preflight on subset of nodes due to a race in the upgrade job (missing fencing for concurrent node provisioning).
- immediate mitigations applied: traffic-shift to us-west-2, forced preflight+restart on affected nodes, cordon/drain pattern.
- observed impact: ~12 dedicated jobs delayed 3–12 minutes, no data loss, 1 customer reported tail-latency spike.

katie (eng-sre): post-incident runbook updates I propose:
- add a preflight gate that fails rollout on nodes if /opt/nvidia/preflight-check.sh returns nonzero (do not mark node as ready for GPU until pass).
- update playbook step to check for 'driver version mismatch' as a distinct alarm and map to a dedicated remediation path.
- add a quick jq command block (from raj) into runbook for fast node detection.

raj (eng-runtime): longer-term changes:
- introduce a per-pool driver rollout semaphore so only one upgrade job runs concurrently for GPU pools to avoid race conditions.
- instrument allocatable GPU metric 'node.gpu.allocatable_zeros' and alert when >X nodes report zero allocatable GPUs.

maria (eng-platform): ops/process changes:
- create a warm-pool terraform module for cross-region warm nodes (costed, opt-in for Dedicated customers).
- document cost threshold and approval flow for cross-region failover (so we don't shift traffic automatically without billing or sales ok for big tenants).

luis (eng-ml): eval/action: add perf regression check after cross-region shift to automatically notify product for customer-impacting latency changes.

sam (oncall): immediate action items assigned:
- katie: update runbook with jq snippet + new alarm signatures (ETA end of day).
- raj: add semaphore to the driver-upgrade job and add metric (ETA 2 days).
- maria: prototype warm-pool module + cost doc (ETA 3 days).
- luis: add synthetic latency check for shifted tenants (ETA 1 day).

katie (eng-sre): adding those to the incident board now. ticket numbers: INC-4321 (runbook), INC-4322 (upgrade semaphore), INC-4323 (warm-pool), INC-4324 (perf checks).

sam (oncall): retrospective items (non-blocking):
- consider adding a 'pre-provision warm-pool' option in Dedicated contracts for high-availability customers.
- add short playbook snippet to prefer taint+drain vs immediate cordon for mixed-node pools.

maria (eng-platform): will schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review the warm-pool cost model and opt-in UX with sales.

sam (oncall): thanks all — great triage. closing thread once runbook PR lands. :thumbsup:
